head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy and reduce op count of jax.lax.erfc.

Previously, `erfc` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST` approximated `erfcx(|x|)` in `1 / |x|`. Because `1 / |x|` blows up near `0`, it needed a separate `1 - erf(x)` polynomial for `|x| < 1`, three or four more polynomial pieces across `|x| >= 1`, and two divisions, with `select`s to pick between them (`chlo.erfc`, used for `bfloat16`, similarly evaluates three interval polynomials and two divisions). In vector code every polynomial runs on every input, so most of that work is thrown away.

Shifting the reciprocal to `u = 1 / (|x| + c)` (`c = 2` for `bfloat16` and `float32`, `c = 4` for `float64`) maps all `|x| >= 0` onto `(0, 1/c]` without blowing up at `0`, so a single polynomial `erfc(|x|) = exp(-x^2) * u * P(u)` covers all `x >= 0` (with `2 - erfc(|x|)` for `x < 0`) using one reciprocal and no interval splits.

Enable this new implementation for `float32` and `float64` in `AccuracyMode.HIGHEST`, and for `bfloat16` in all accuracy modes: on `bfloat16`, both `chlo.erfc` and the new implementation are correctly rounded (`<= 0.5` ULP) and bitwise identical on every non-NaN `bfloat16` input across CPU, GPU, and TPU (and both return NaN on NaN inputs), while cutting the StableHLO op count from 63 to 25.

StableHLO operation counts (after expanding `chlo.erfc` and running CSE, excluding constants) and worst-case ULP errors:

| Implementation | Add/Sub/Neg | Mul | Div | Exp | Compare/Select | Other | Total Ops | Max ULP |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| `bfloat16` before (`chlo.erfc`) | 24 | 25 | 2 | 1 | 8 | 3 | 63 | 0.5 |
| `bfloat16` after (default & `HIGHEST`) | 9 | 9 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 25 | 0.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` before | 43 | 40 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 105 | 4.0–5.5 |
| `float32` `HIGHEST` after | 44 | 35 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 6 | 88 | 1.5 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` before | 84 | 80 | 2 | 1 | 12 | 7 | 186 | 2.5–3.0 |
| `float64` `HIGHEST` after | 79 | 53 | 1 | 0 | 2 | 12 | 147 | 2.0 |
